_note: PROPOSED changes only, for later review by the ledger owner. Nothing here edits the canonical model or dashboard, and nothing assigns or changes a conviction. Anchor IDs are used only where the mapping is clear; otherwise target_claim_id is null and research_question_ids identify the scope. Evidence IDs resolve to evidence.json. supporting_evidence_ids and challenging_evidence_ids are relative to the PROPOSED wording or qualification, not the original ledger claim (corrected after the final fidelity check, FC-26 to FC-29).

revision_candidates.proposed_wording_or_qualification: Split the claim. (a) Accountability sustains a non-delegable evaluation core — deciding, vetting the producer's competence and independence, judging whether the work is sufficient, following up red flags, and building a record of one's own investigation. This core persists regardless of the advisor's transparency, but in most regimes it does not require re-performing the advisor's work. (b) Opacity may add re-derivation on top of that core. The mechanism is supported; its share of recipient effort is unmeasured. Note also that regulators more often observe under-review of outside specialists than excessive review. Where recipient review visibly fell in credit (appraisal), the mechanism was transfer of risk to the consequence-bearer, not greater transparency.
revision_candidates.rationale: Round 2 reviewers agreed the obligation core is well evidenced (33 evidence groups at Round 1; 35 'supports' groups for P1.1 in the final register) and that the size of the opacity-driven component is unmeasured. The Round 2 audit asked that P1.1 be split into 'obligation exists' and 'obligation is the dominant driver'. Round 3 legal doctrine located the line between relying on outside work and having to investigate independently (red flags; content certified by an expert).
revision_candidates.unresolved_user_judgment: Whether 'repeated review' in the ledger refers to excessive review (where opacity is the lever) or to misdirected review (detail-checking while assumptions go unchallenged), and whether CL027 should treat under-review as part of the same claim.

revision_candidates.proposed_wording_or_qualification: Customer-specific requirements (own P-cases, haircuts, coverage tests, house memo templates, materiality) are one of three co-explanations for continued internal diligence. The other two are non-delegable obligation (W1) and rational discounting of biased advisor forecasts (W3). In renewable project finance, lender adaptation is largely set before detailed diligence and is justified by measured forecast bias, so it is not uniquely explained by customer-specific requirements.
revision_candidates.rationale: Reviewer B noted CL025 is supported but not uniquely identified. Round 3 target-domain evidence (lender account, wind back-test, rating action) shows adaptation is tied to forecast bias. No registered item challenges the qualified wording.
revision_candidates.unresolved_user_judgment: Whether CL025 should explicitly name W1 and W3 as rival explanations, or whether that belongs in a separate claim.

revision_candidates.proposed_wording_or_qualification: Customers should see what was checked, including checks without findings, provided the coverage record is (i) verifiable — traceable to underlying samples or data and recomputable; (ii) right-sized — the nature and scope of each test rather than sample-level detail; (iii) paired with an accountable conclusion, not a findings-only list; and (iv) designed to expose omissions, not only to cite inputs. Current evidence supports coverage records as the way professional systems allocate reliance and as a driver of report completeness. It does not yet show that they improve recipients' detection or reduce recipients' effort. Behavioural evidence adds that design and timing matter. Generic lists or decomposition used as the method of review were associated with lower fraud-risk assessments and poorer detection (abstract-level evidence). Specific documentation, lists consulted after the reviewer's own first read, and coverage focused on how key assumptions were derived helped. Records should therefore be deal-specific, state exclusions and how sensitive each check was, and be consulted after an independent read.
revision_candidates.rationale: Reviewer A called this the thesis's strongest ground, but normative. Reviewer B called it mostly mandates or producer-side completeness. Round 3 doctrine shows procedure disclosures do not move the recipient's duty, and recipients reportedly want negative assurance. Prefilled 'normal' text produced contradictions. Round 3 (R3E) split the dispute by design and timing. No study tests 'checked, no findings' against silence on recipients' detection (DIS004).
revision_candidates.unresolved_user_judgment: Whether the ledger wants CL026 as a design principle (normative) or as an empirical claim about customer benefit. The evidence supports the former more than the latter.

revision_candidates.proposed_wording_or_qualification: Add evidence and specify what implementation involves. Analog evidence shows customer-specific deployment requires configuring recipient criteria (P-cases, haircuts, materiality), templates, data formats, and locally required elements beyond a shared core. Shared national templates covered only 17–49% of one centre's report content, and within-organization standardization needed all users to vet each template.
revision_candidates.rationale: Both reviewers judged CL029 supported by analogy. No target-domain implementation-effort data exist.
revision_candidates.unresolved_user_judgment: How much of the configuration burden is one-time (per customer) vs recurring (per deal); no evidence distinguishes these.

revision_candidates.proposed_wording_or_qualification: Mark the value-capture link as untested by public evidence, and add two cautions. (1) Recipients appear to value an accountable conclusion (negative assurance or opinion) over a findings-only report — one practitioner source. (2) Moving into the recipient's own judgment — drafting substantive memo content — risks anchoring the recipient on the advisor's conclusions and reducing scrutiny, and memos written by external consultants were flagged as a governance concern.
revision_candidates.rationale: Both reviewers found no evidence on value capture. Round 3 added professional evidence that integrated drafts import judgment and lower skepticism.
revision_candidates.unresolved_user_judgment: Whether 'beyond findings' in CL007 means accountable conclusions (supported as recipient preference) or integration into the recipient's decision materials (where the risks apply). These have different evidence profiles.

revision_candidates.proposed_wording_or_qualification: Board, IC and memo preparation burden is stated, not measured. Memo templates differ across investors, and writing plus review averages about two months (interview-based). The effort is customer-specific. In one government trial, AI assistance for slide production was faster but scored much lower on accuracy. Treat as plausible adjacent demand with unquantified size.
revision_candidates.rationale: No source quantifies preparation or reformatting time. Board-pack sources are vendor-linked. The literature on investment memos is essentially absent.
revision_candidates.unresolved_user_judgment: Whether K001 refers to the recipient's own reporting upward (board packs) or to integrating advisor outputs into IC memos. The evidence differs.

revision_candidates.proposed_wording_or_qualification: No public evidence tests whether reduced verification effort converts into paid demand. Available evidence shows purchase decisions resting on satisfaction or break-even framing rather than measured effort reduction, and perceived time savings diverging from measured ones. In the appraisal case, effort reduction from standardized, machine-checkable outside analysis accrued mainly to recipients and the consequence-bearer, not the producer.
revision_candidates.rationale: Reviewer B: stated pain only. Reviewer A: unsupported. No disagreement.
revision_candidates.unresolved_user_judgment: What observation would count as conversion evidence for this ledger (e.g., renewal tied to measured review hours).

revision_candidates.proposed_wording_or_qualification: Split 'assets repeat' from 'economics repeat'. Analog evidence supports a standardizable core of deliverable content with substantial local additions, and judgment that stays variable even with a shared vocabulary. No public evidence addresses whether supplier economics repeat. In the one credit-domain case found (US appraisal), standardization plus machine-checkability made the homogeneous tier repeatable enough to be intermediated and partly replaced by waivers. Producers faced fee pressure; complex or heterogeneous assets kept bespoke work.
revision_candidates.rationale: Round 2: Reviewer A said formats only; Reviewer B said challenged. Round 3 (R3F) found that, in appraisal, standardization coincided with commoditization and substitution; the gains went to recipients and the consequence-bearer (DIS007, resolved at the level framed).
revision_candidates.unresolved_user_judgment: Whether AS06 is meant at the level of reusable content/assets or of unit economics.

revision_candidates.proposed_wording_or_qualification: New candidate: the value of traceability depends on granularity and on where the error sits. Claim- and calculation-level links to correct sources can cut verification time while preserving detection of errors in the linked facts. Links can increase acceptance of errors in reasoning or computation. Value must be measured as detection on producer-wrong cases, never as trust or satisfaction.
revision_candidates.rationale: This is the narrowed version of the thesis that both Round 2 reviewers could accept (DIS003). Supporting experiments are lay or bundled-professional, and the error-location distinction is synthesized from two lay studies.
revision_candidates.unresolved_user_judgment: Whether to hold this as a working design principle pending a professional seeded-error study.

revision_candidates.proposed_wording_or_qualification: New candidate: integrating advisor *evidence* into the recipient's working system at the point of use moderately reduces regeneration of that evidence. Integrating advisor *judgments* into decision materials risks anchoring and reduced scrutiny unless provenance and development documentation travel with them.
revision_candidates.rationale: Round 3 (R3D) replicated the integration effect beyond one site, at moderate size, with offsets. R3A and R3D added evidence that inherited analysis is scrutinized less.
revision_candidates.unresolved_user_judgment: Whether the ledger's integration thesis targets W5 assembly, W2 regeneration, or memo content. The evidence supports the first two more than the third.

revision_candidates.proposed_wording_or_qualification: New candidate (renewable project finance): in the public record (one lender presentation, one rating action, one DFI terms of reference, one securitization report), lenders' retained energy-yield work consists of adaptation (own P-cases, haircuts, sizing rules), with parallel assessments listed but not quantified. The lender justifies this by forecast bias; that the adaptation responds to bias is analyst inference. In public scopes, review of the sponsor's yield assessment is largely bought from the independent engineer. Better-documented IE reports would not by themselves remove haircuts; back-tested accuracy evidence bears on them more directly. Traceability benefits may land first at the IE and second at the lender.
revision_candidates.rationale: Round 3 (R3C) target-domain documents. Evidence is thin: one lender presentation, one DFI terms of reference (biogas), one securitization report, mostly wind back-tests. IEA PVPS notes that additional assessments are requested when results are unclear, which is opacity-driven and cuts the other way.
revision_candidates.unresolved_user_judgment: Whether the ledger's target customer is the lender, the IE, or the sponsor. The location of the traceability benefit differs.

revision_candidates.proposed_wording_or_qualification: New candidate: in the legal doctrine examined, a recipient may rely without re-performing only on accountable, expert-certified content, and only absent red flags. Disclosure of procedures and findings is evidence the recipient can cite, but it does not discharge the recipient's duty to judge sufficiency, follow up red flags, and build its own record. Reports that read as products without an accountable, consenting expert leave that duty intact.
revision_candidates.rationale: Round 3 (R3B). This is doctrine, not observed effort, and US securities and Delaware law do not govern private lenders or ICs directly.
revision_candidates.unresolved_user_judgment: Whether renewable-energy lender and IC credit policies mirror this structure. Policy documents would be needed.
